rows.prompt: I’m organizing a wedding weekend with 42 guests, two venues, and transportation constraints. Events: welcome dinner Fri 7–10pm, ceremony Sat 3–4pm, reception Sat 5–11pm, farewell brunch Sun 10am–12pm. Constraints: venue A is 25 minutes from venue B; we have one shuttle (14 seats) that can do continuous loops but must have a 10-minute loading buffer at each stop; 10 guests are staying at a hotel near venue A, 20 near venue B, 12 at an Airbnb halfway (15 minutes from both). Everyone must arrive by event start; no one should wait more than 30 minutes after an event ends for a ride. Build a shuttle timetable for all events and tell me how many trips are needed in each window.

Paragraph:
After a decade of planning, the coastal city approved a new flood protection strategy. Instead of building one massive seawall, officials chose a layered approach: restoring wetlands, elevating roads, and adding removable barriers near the harbor. Construction will begin next spring with drainage upgrades in the most vulnerable neighborhood, followed by wetland restoration over the next two years. Business groups supported the plan because it avoids blocking waterfront views, while some residents worry the project will take too long. The city will reassess progress annually using updated sea-level projections.

There are 7 people in a logic club. Each person is either a “day-knight” (truthful on weekdays, lies on weekends) or a “night-knave” (lies on weekdays, truthful on weekends). Today is either Friday, Saturday, or Sunday. They make these statements:
P: “Today is Saturday.”
Q: “R is a night-knave.”
R: “S is a day-knight.”
S: “T is a day-knight.”
T: “U is a night-knave.”
U: “P is a night-knave.”
V: “Today is Friday.”
Assuming at least one statement is true and at least one is false, determine what day it is and classify each person if possible, or explain why it’s underdetermined.
A fair coin is flipped until two consecutive heads occur. What is the expected number of flips? Show your reasoning.

Paragraph:
A mid-sized hospital introduced an AI tool to help prioritize radiology scans, flagging images that might show internal bleeding or a collapsed lung. Doctors said it sometimes sped up care for critical patients, especially overnight, but they also reported false alarms that disrupted workflow. The vendor trained the model on data from large academic centers, and staff worried it might miss patterns common in their local population. The hospital created a review committee, required human sign-off for all decisions, and began tracking error rates by age and ethnicity to check for bias.

FROM orders o

Paragraph:
In 2024, several universities reported a sharp increase in students seeking mental health support, with some counseling centers booking appointments three weeks out. Administrators blamed a mix of academic pressure, financial stress, and lingering social disruption from the pandemic years. To respond, campuses expanded group therapy, trained faculty to recognize warning signs, and contracted with telehealth providers for after-hours care. Critics argue that outsourcing can fragment support and raise privacy concerns. Early data from one campus showed a 18% drop in crisis walk-ins after adding same-day triage, but wait times for regular therapy remained a challenge.

Constraints: each person works 5 shifts per week, no more than 3 consecutive days, at least 12 hours between shifts, everyone must do at least 2 opens and 2 closes across the 2 weeks, and weekends must be fairly shared (no one works both Saturday and Sunday in the same week). Paragraph:
Our community garden started as a vacant lot filled with weeds and broken glass. A few neighbors met on a Saturday, brought gloves and trash bags, and cleared the space. Over the next months we built raised beds from reclaimed wood, tested the soil, and planted tomatoes, beans, and herbs. People who had never spoken before began swapping tools and recipes. Kids painted signs for each plot, and older residents taught pruning and composting. The harvest wasn’t huge, but it changed the block: fewer people littered, more people walked by, and the lot became a place to talk rather than avoid.
